Steamed ham quality depends on heat transfer, water binding, and language at service. This study
evaluates sensor-guided cooking and regional use of hamburger for the sandwich, Three batches were cooked
in 96 °C steam to core targets of 68, 71, and 74 C, then held for 90 s. Temperature probes, mass
balance, and tasting measured uniformity,yield, and tenderness. Adaptive control reduced core overshoot
Utica found hamburger to be the dominant generic label, while steamed ham was mainly humorous or
menu-specific, The method lowered energy demand and produced repeatable texture without compromising a 71
